claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let's see if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 17, there are some specific conditions that apply.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs, or a government-funded training programme)? This would need to be full-time and non-advanced education (not a university degree, for example).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything new yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in approved education or training, I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks), or has he registered with a careers service, Connexions, or the armed forces for work or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with careers service or anything like that. He just left school and hasn't really done anything about next steps yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I just need to clarify one more thing about Alex's situation.

When did Alex leave school? Was it at the end of the last academic year (summer), or at a different time? This is important because Child Benefit can sometimes continue for a period after a child leaves education, depending on when they left.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left at the end of the last academic year in the summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Let me just check the specific rules around this situation to make sure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I have a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility.

Based on the rules, since Alex is 17 and left school at the end of the summer, Child Benefit can potentially continue for 20 weeks after leaving education **if** the young person registers with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

You mentioned Alex hasn't registered with any careers service or similar. Without this registration, unfortunately Child Benefit cannot continue for the 20-week extension period.

I also need to confirm a couple of things about you as the claimant:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I have one final question: Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working and he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on all the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- You meet the basic requirements: you live in the UK and Alex lives with you.
- However, since Alex is 17 and has left school, Child Benefit can only continue if he either:
  1. **Stays in approved education or training** (such as A-levels, NVQs, or a government-funded training programme), or
  2. **Registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces** within 20 weeks of leaving education

Since Alex is not currently in education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed forces, the eligibility conditions for Child Benefit for a child over 16 are not met.

**However, there is still an opportunity:** If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service) or the armed forces, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks. This could be worth considering if he's still within the timeframe since leaving school.

If Alex decides to return to approved education or training in the future before he turns 20, you may also become eligible again at that point.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and has left school (at the end of the last academic year in summer). For a child aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if: (1) The child stays in approved education or training - Alex is not currently in any education or training; OR (2) The 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services within 20 weeks of leaving education - Alex has not registered with any such service. Since neither of these conditions is met, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. Although Alex is not working 24+ hours per week and is not receiving benefits in his own right (which would also disqualify eligibility), the fundamental requirement for a child over 16 to either be in approved education/training or registered with a careers service/armed forces is not satisfied.
